# Instrument engineering first study

`first-observations.json` retains all 67 original files, their modes and SHA-256
identities. Eight binary QLV2 packets use base64; UTF-8 records retain their
original text. Recorded paths, commands and the host driver are inert history.
The static reader never executes them or follows their recorded paths.

Five first sources precede checking. Three initially fail at current import/name
resolution; separate import translations preserve those failures. All five
supported translations pass selected Raw checking, while source emission rejects
the open entries. The five native bodies are independently hand-authored
translations, not emitted artifacts or source-preservation evidence. The existing
exact instrument gate accepts five self-comparisons and rejects three unequal
pairs. Its unsupported epsilon-extension refusal is preserved separately.

Independent exact host algebra gives a Unit-input positive witness with bound
1/2 and rejects 1/4. A residual-qubit case has coefficient majorant sum 2, despite
its true complete adjoint bound 1/2; the sufficient witness is conservative.
Reset and identity on half of a Bell pair have identical public probabilities
but different residual/reference coherence. These are bounded observations,
separate from new engineering checking, general proofs and constitutional PR/RS.

Maximum physical live width is two qubits. No new maximum-size case, coefficient
domain, source phase/const feature, guarantee admission or Issue completion is
claimed. First records remain unchanged; later validation belongs separately.
